name: Myanmar

findings.local_actor: Naypyidaw Safe City (Myanmar government; integrators Linn IT Solutions, Nang Yoe)
findings.summary: First phase of Naypyidaw Safe City went live with 335 cameras across eight townships, equipment mostly Huawei, with facial and licence-plate recognition alerting authorities; HRW cites a US$1.2 million project value.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei told HRW the recognition software is not its product and it does not operate the system; who supplies and can update the analytics layer is unconfirmed. Tier 5 reflects operational status, though scale is one city. Two S3 sources, no S1/S2, so uncorroborated.

findings.summary: Mandalay Safe City camera system agreed with Huawei before the 2021 coup; Reuters reported at least 300 Huawei cameras installed before the coup, with hundreds more planned and the junta pressing for faster rollout.
findings.analyst_inference: HRW gives the Mandalay project as announced in 2019 at about US$1.24 million; not entered as a value because HRW reports it second-hand. Reuters could not verify installations on site. Audit 2026-10-22: Cameras were installed before the Feb 2021 coup, not by mid-2022.

findings.local_actor: Myanmar junta city administrations; integrators Fisca Security & Communication, Naung Yoe Technologies
findings.summary: After the coup, camera-surveillance tenders in Mawlamyine, Taunggyi and Dawei went to local integrators installing hundreds of Dahua cameras; Dahua cameras also reported in Myitkyina, with plans for every state and region.
findings.analyst_inference: Single Reuters report; Reuters itself could not verify tenders or installations. Same report notes a Hikvision traffic command centre in Yangon, which Hikvision says it did not sell directly to government; not coded separately.

findings.local_actor: Myanmar junta / Ministry of Transport and Communications; 13 operators incl. MPT, ATOM, Mytel, Ooredoo Myanmar
findings.summary: Leaked Geedge Networks data, reviewed by a media and NGO coalition, indicates the firm supplied the junta a commercial censorship and subscriber-tracking system tied into Myanmar operators' networks, covering tens of millions of internet users.

sources.publisher: Follow the Money / Great Firewall Export project

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3 is conservative: the leak suggests a delivered, functioning system (possibly tier 5), but deployment status per operator is not independently confirmed. RFA (2024) relayed earlier JFM claims about leaked plans, including a CEIEC location-tracking proposal; RFA treated as S4 as US state-funded.

findings.local_actor: Telenor Myanmar (now ATOM; buyers M1 Group, Lebanon, and Shwe Byain Phyu)
findings.reversal_of: Telenor's ownership and operation of Telenor Myanmar, a nationwide mobile operator
findings.summary: Telenor got final regulatory approval to sell its Myanmar unit to Lebanon's M1 Group with local partner Shwe Byain Phyu, citing the post-coup security situation and conflict between local and European law.
findings.analyst_inference: Mobile World Live gives the sale price as US$105 million; not entered as a value because it is the price of the exit, not of a stack commitment. Shwe Byain Phyu was to take a majority of the buying vehicle, so operator control shifts toward domestic owners.

findings.reversal_of: Ooredoo's ownership and operation of Ooredoo Myanmar, a nationwide mobile operator
findings.summary: Ooredoo agreed to sell its Myanmar unit, founded 2014, to Singapore-based Nine Communications, making it the second foreign-owned operator to leave post-coup Myanmar; closing was subject to Myanmar regulatory approval.
findings.analyst_inference: Reported price about US$576 million (estimate), not entered. Closing date not confirmed in sources seen. Developing Telecoms item seen in search results, not fetched. Audit 2026-10-22: the sale is reported completed and the operator rebranded as U9 on 20 Sep 2025 (lead only; closing date unconfirmed). Audit 2026-10-22: no longer corroborated, because a second source was seen only as a search-result headline.

findings.local_actor: Scam compounds on the Thai-Myanmar border (unlicensed users)
findings.reversal_of: Starlink service to terminals operating at suspected scam centres in Myanmar
findings.summary: SpaceX said it identified and disabled more than 2,500 Starlink kits near suspected scam centres in Myanmar, after a military raid on KK Park seized Starlink terminals.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 assigned because the reversed service was unlicensed, small-scale use rather than a sanctioned deployment; Starlink's licensing status in Myanmar is not stated in the sources. Only NBC fetched; others seen in search results. Audit 2026-10-22: no longer corroborated, because a second source was seen only as a search-result headline.

findings.local_actor: Earthquake rescue responders and local authorities
findings.summary: After the March 2025 earthquake, a DeepSeek-based Chinese–Burmese translation platform was used to help international rescuers communicate with local authorities, reportedly assisting over 700 people.
findings.analyst_inference: Emergency, donor-side use; not evidence of Myanmar government adoption of a PRC model. Claim rests on CCTV reporting relayed by the source.

facilities.null_reason: one search found only pre-2023 Yangon data-centre projects; no AI or large data-centre project since 2023 surfaced; trade.gov (Sept 2026) notes limited local computing capacity

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; Myanmar is D:5 with presumption of denial (global layer) and no accelerator purchase surfaced in other searches

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on surveillance and network layers
